description: External differential ratchet for Orrery. The verify-external/ layer cross-checks the unmodified core against an independent astrodynamics library (hapsira 0.18.0, the maintained poliastro fork) plus scipy and cited closed forms, and against committed JPL Horizons fixtures, offline and deterministically from a fixed seed. Each entry has a current value (the worst agreement error observed in a real external run, or null before the first run) and a target (the asserted tolerance, traced to a source). Targets for exact methods are anchored to the core's own measured internal envelope in bar.json plus oracle-method headroom; targets for approximate models are the model's published accuracy envelope, never machine precision. Current values move toward target only through verified runs. Every current below was produced by the committed run shown in the turn STATUS block. No number here is fabricated.
pinnedOracle: hapsira==0.18.0 (poliastro fork); scipy and cited closed forms for the pieces hapsira does not cover; resolved dependency versions in requirements.lock
seedPolicy: Engine outputs are emitted by verify-external/sample/emit.ts from the per-category integer seeds in sample/seeds.ts (recorded in each generated JSON). The core's xoshiro256** generator and the forbidden wall-clock and nondeterministic-random rules make a fixed input reproducible; the external sample uses its own fixed seed. After the one-time Horizons fixture fetch, the entire suite runs offline against committed fixtures.

standishVsHorizons.unit: relative (max heliocentric position error of the Standish model over all fixtures)
standishVsHorizons.source: JPL Keplerian Elements for Approximate Positions of the Major Planets (Standish), 1800-2050 envelope; two-tier STANDISH_POS_RTOL_TERRESTRIAL 1e-3 and STANDISH_POS_RTOL_GIANT 4e-3 in tests/tolerances.py
standishVsHorizons.note: planetStateAtJD (Curtis Algorithm 8.1) vs committed Horizons heliocentric ecliptic J2000 geometric vectors. Approximate model: held to its published envelope, never to engine precision. current 3.27e-3 is Saturn (the Jupiter-Saturn great inequality this low-precision set omits), within the 4e-3 giant tier. Earth and Mars (anchored to the core constants) worst is 3.37e-4, within the 1e-3 terrestrial tier. The exact per-planet published arcsecond figures are pending source re-verification; the two tiers are conservative ceilings labeled as such.

elementsVsLibrary.source: bar.json keplerRoundTripError 8.7e-14 internal envelope + hapsira rv2coe/coe2rv float ordering; ELEMENTS_FWD_RTOL / ELEMENTS_INV_RTOL
elementsVsLibrary.note: rvToElements and coeToRv vs hapsira rv2coe and coe2rv on the same SI input, 1024 cases per direction. Forward worst 2.13e-14, inverse worst 8.80e-14.

keplerVsLibrary.source: bar.json universalVsRegimeError 7.0e-14 internal envelope + hapsira danby cutoff; KEPLER_RTOL
keplerVsLibrary.note: propagateUniversal vs hapsira danby (converged to 1e-13) on the same input, 1024 cases. Worst 2.89e-13.

lambertVsLibrary.source: bar.json lambertIzzoVsBmwError 4.4e-13 internal envelope + third-library Izzo cutoff; LAMBERT_VEL_RTOL
lambertVsLibrary.note: lambertIzzo vs hapsira core izzo, 1024 cases. Single-revolution worst 1.92e-14; multi-revolution (revs 1 and 2, both branches per revolution count, engine rightBranch mapped to hapsira lowpath) worst 1.04e-14. The cross-propagator endpoint re-propagation (engine v1 through hapsira farnocchia reaching r2) worst is 6.53e-10 within LAMBERT_ENDPOINT_RTOL 1e-7.

maneuversVsLibrary.source: hapsira Maneuver (hohmann, bielliptic) and cited closed forms (plane change, combined); correctly-rounded arithmetic; MANEUVER_DV_RTOL
maneuversVsLibrary.note: hohmann and biElliptic vs hapsira.core.maneuver; planeChange and combinedPlaneChange vs the cited closed form, 1024 cases. Worst total-delta-v agreement 4.62e-15.

lagrangeVsLibrary.source: bar.json lagrangeL4L5Error 4.7e-16 and collinearResidual 2.95e-14 + scipy brentq and hapsira mapping headroom; LAGRANGE_COLLINEAR_RTOL / LAGRANGE_EQUILATERAL_RTOL
lagrangeVsLibrary.note: lagrangePoints vs hapsira.threebody.restricted.lagrange_points (worst 1.89e-12), an independent scipy.optimize.brentq collinear root (worst 2.89e-14), and the exact equilateral closed form for L4/L5 (worst 0.0), 1024 cases. The |dOmega/dx| residual at the engine collinear points stays under LAGRANGE_COLLINEAR_RESIDUAL_ATOL 1e-12.

patchedConicVsReference.source: patched-conic published envelope PATCHED_CONIC_VINF_RTOL 1e-3 (bar.json earthMarsVinfError target 1e-3); the recorded current is the differential agreement of two exact Lambert solvers, far inside that envelope
patchedConicVsReference.note: transferArc (engine Bate-Mueller-White heliocentric Lambert arc) vs an independent hapsira izzo solve of the same arc, compared on the departure and arrival hyperbolic excess speed v_inf, 1024 cases. Worst 5.97e-12. Held to the approximate patched-conic published envelope 1e-3, never to machine precision; the tight 5.97e-12 current is the two exact solvers agreeing, not the model-vs-reality accuracy.

shortspanVsHorizons.unit: relative (max heliocentric position error of short-span two-body propagation)
shortspanVsHorizons.source: two-body short-span truncation envelope SHORTSPAN_POS_RTOL 2e-5 (and SHORTSPAN_VEL_RTOL 1e-3 for velocity); committed fixtures/horizons_shortspan.json
shortspanVsHorizons.note: Oracle A second check: propagateUniversal of a real Horizons heliocentric state (km, km/s, MU_SUN) against the real Horizons state 2, 10, or 40 days later. Worst position 5.19e-6 relative (Mars, 40 day span), worst velocity 1.82e-4 relative. Pure two-body neglects each planet's own GM and all third-body perturbation; the disagreement is the two-body model truncation, which scales as span^2 in position (measured 40d/2d ratio 462) and linearly in velocity, never tightened to engine precision.

fixtureCount.unit: count (committed Horizons planet bodies, one or more epochs each)
fixtureCount.source: all eight major planet-system barycenters covered by committed JPL Horizons fixtures and the data/standish_all_planets.json element tables
fixtureCount.note: Eight bodies (barycenters 1 through 8) at four epochs each, 32 records, committed in fixtures/horizons_planets.json for the Standish check. The Oracle A short-span check adds fixtures/horizons_shortspan.json, the same eight bodies at three short spans each (24 state pairs). Earth and Mars also anchor to the in-core STANDISH_EARTH/STANDISH_MARS; the other six come from the cited data file fed to the unmodified planetStateAtJD.

sampleSize.unit: count (nominal seeded cases per analytic category)
sampleSize.note: 1024 nominal cases per analytic category (elements forward and inverse, kepler, lambert, maneuvers, lagrange, patchedconic). The fixture-bound categories stay fixture-sized (standish 32 records, shortspan 24 pairs). The adversarial profile adds 128 concentrated break-push cases per analytic category for the break runs.

unexplainedDisagreements.source: verification rule: every cross-implementation disagreement above tolerance is either a filed failing test (a counterexample) or an explained, cited model-accuracy gap
unexplainedDisagreements.note: The committed nominal run (14 tests, 1024 cases per analytic category) passes with zero disagreements above tolerance, and three consecutive break pushes on distinct adversarial samples (seed-offset rounds 1, 2, 3) each pass 14/14 with zero new unexplained disagreements. The adversarial survey surfaced one cross-implementation disagreement (hyperbolic Kepler), explained as an oracle-domain limit: hapsira danby solves the elliptic and parabolic Kepler equation only and wraps the hyperbolic mean anomaly mod 2pi, so the hyperbolic oracle is the robust all-conic farnocchia, which confirms the engine to 1e-13. The two approximate-model gaps are explained, not unexplained: Saturn 3.27e-3 against the giant-planet Standish envelope, and the short-span two-body position error 5.19e-6 against the two-body truncation envelope (it scales as span^2, the perturbation signature).
